disputes_adjudicated.reason: Fix holds. src/regex_pattern.cpp now has pop_last_utf8_codepoint(), which walks back over UTF-8 continuation bytes (mask 0xC0==0x80) to find the true lead byte before trimming, instead of popping one byte. Re-derived the original repro against the fixed code: extract_required_literal("\xF0\x9F\x98\x80?xyz", 3) now correctly returns "xyz" with no stray emoji bytes, and CompiledRegex confirms the plain line "xyz" still matches. Mutation check: reverted pop_last_utf8_codepoint back to a plain current_run.pop_back(), rebuilt, and the new regression test failed exactly as expected. Reverted the mutation; full suite is clean again.

Fix holds. src/alias_manager.cpp now copies `Action action = a->action;` and `bool fall_through = a->opts.fall_through;` out of the vector entry before invoking the callback, mirroring TriggerManager::process_line. The regression test was strengthened exactly as HANDOFF claims: it removes itself then adds 500 aliases from inside the callback. Ran clean under ASan with the fix in place. Reverted the fix in a clone (restored the raw-pointer invocation), rebuilt, and reran: reproduced a real heap-buffer-overflow via ASan, the same failure mode round 1 found. Reverted the mutation; ASan build is clean again.

Fix holds and closes the coverage gap. The new test deliberately races pause() against a 2ms repeating timer's own deadline across 20 trials, watching 8 interval-widths afterward, and asserts leaked ticks <= 20. Independently removed the generation check in handle_fire, rebuilt, and ran just this test -- it failed clearly (126 leaked ticks vs. threshold 20, ~6x overshoot), confirming real coverage. Reverted the mutation; full release suite (102/102) passes again with the real check restored.
